lines.en: Maya Makinami never thought she’d enjoy life as a cuck. But she was kind of almost starting to except for all of the parts where she wasn’t. Which was most of them.
Regardless, she stood there in all of her cucky glory with a cucky broom in her cucky hands and thought to herself - ”What am I going to eat for dinner?”

But then after that, she thought - ”Can this state of being, so dissimilar from the life I once envisioned for myself, truly become something I can grow to appreciate and, perhaps, even love? The same way I love him?”
The latter thought was significantly more complicated than the first.

So complicated, in fact, that as the hands of The Millennium Clock ticked incessantly back and forth between The Martyr and The Old Clown, she was still, after all this time, incapable of coming up with an answer.
But it was an answer she must arrive at for any of this to matter at all, you see.
She was important.

Far more important than us. Than those who watch from the tiled floors in the National Museum of Scotland in great awe of the bell who sits atop The Spire, wanting to touch it, but knowing they never will.

But what if, on some lazy Sunday, a fit of madness consumed this rhetorical person? And what if that person, naked as the day they were born, sprinted through the halls that house time itself and destroyed it all?
What if they made it to the clock, felt the power of God course through them like It were the first sip of a Five Hour Energy, then surpassed human limits and destroyed the destruction of man?
I think that, in such an oddly specific and mildly irreverent scenario, we’d have a real shot at eclectic, blissful anarchy in this little anthill of ours.

But, as it stands, the way we are is Pandora’s Box. And despite the Hunger, Madness, and Grief, we’re all just Intellectuals and Hermits on the way to War Camps to partake in Forced Labor in the name of today’s Holocaust.
This War, Invalid as it may seem, has its bright spots though.

The Belfry shines beneath The Requiem, bathing us in awe, in solitude, in want of something like this to extend beyond the reaches of what governs us and compel us to finish our opening narrations so that a bunch of girls in cute outfits can show up and bother the subject of today’s troubles.
Just...
It wouldn’t really be bothersome at all.
For despite the loneliness of the shrine maiden, there was also a painful yearning.
The same kind that used to wish for windows just to realize that, should those windows exist, all she’d see is darkness. Even three stories up.
That was all she knew before the light found her.
And, like clockwork, that was also all he knew before the light found him.
: Okay, everyone! Single file line! We need to look as cool as possible so that Maya welcomes us with open arms.
: Huh? What’s-
: Oh, absolutely fucking not.
: Well, if it isn’t everyone’s favorite miko in the flesh! Strike a pose, gang. And say something cool so it looks like we belong here!
: Sup. Come here often?
: So this is what it’s like here. Interesting. It feels less oppressive and far more serene than I expected.
: Yumi? Are you-
: Shut the fuck up, Four Eyes. Just...completely ignore that I’m even here until all of this embarrassing shit is over and done with.
: Ayane...I don’t know what you think you’re doing, but-
: You know, it wasn’t all that long ago that a wise woman looked at me and said — “Ayane...One day, if something terrible happens to me, it will be you who must carry the mantle.”
: “For it is only through teamwork, persistence, acceptance of one another, and an abundance of miko dresses that this world can truly be saved. I love you so much. We’ll be best friends forever.”
: And that wise woman, Maya?...That wise woman was you.
: No it fucking wasn’t. No iteration of me would ever say “I love you so much. We’ll be best friends forever.”
: You said it with your eyes.
: And I will never forget the look. Because-
: Go away! And take everyone else with you! None of you are allowed to be here!
: What do you mean? Of course we are. Shrines are public property protected by the Japanese government.
: Well, this one isn’t! And parading a bunch of false shrine maidens here under the guise of volunteers or whatever the fuck this is is just going to make the gods angry!
: But cursing in their very home will not? Also, you don’t even believe in God. You used to tell me all the time between reminding me that we are best friends who will be together forever.
: Does anyone else want those two to date or is it just me?
: I think our class would be best if it was just one massive polycule where, each day, we drew a randomized partner out of a hat and started anew the following morning.
: The fuck are we even doing here again? I blacked out the second Blondie told me how much she’d pay me to put on this stupid fucking dress.
: Some sort of meeting she used to do before the first iteration of Maya was wiped from existence. I was never informed as to why the shouzoku was necessary, though.
: Wait, wiped from existence? The heck you talkin’ about with this “wiped from existence” nonsense? Sensei never told me about that.

: Right, so, despite living in a never-ending loop of our freshman year, we can technically still lose whatever memories we accumulate throughout said loops and wind up back at the starting point. That happened to Maya.
: What?! Don’t you think that’s something somebody should’ve told me before I started rewriting my outlook on life to be a lot more optimistic?!
: This changes everything! And I literally just changed, Makoto! Both literally and figuratively!
: You’re going to have to get used to a lot of caveats and information that slips through the cracks from here on out if you want to survive, Uta. That’s just how it is here.
: And this “starting point” is where, exactly?
: It changes all the time. Just somewhere near the beginning of the school year for the most part.
: And I assume the only memories that are purged are the ones we’ve made during the loops and not those that predate when they began, correct?
: Pretty much, yeah. Good job.
: This was some sort of ritual then? That Ayane and Maya conducted to try and prevent such a thing from happening with the assistance of this shrine’s deity?
: No. I think Ayane just liked wearing the dress and hanging out with Maya, to be honest.
: For the last time, go home!
: Maya, calm down! We’re not going to bother you! If anything, we’re here to help! Sweeping this whole place by yourself must get pretty exhausting, right?
: Not really! Nobody ever comes here and I mostly just walk around and internally monologue about how shitty my life is until Sensei shows up and I get to make fun of him instead!
: Well, consider today an exciting shake-up of your regular formula then!
: It’s like I was saying earlier — if we’re ever going to make it through this, we must do it with the power of friendship. Right, gang? For it is only with each other’s assistance that we can ever-
: Ayane. A word. In private.
: I’m sorry Maya, but I already have a boyfriend.
: Not that kind of word!
: A threesome then? I suppose I’m okay with that. But we must first establish some ground rules and come up with a safe word.
: That’s it! Everyone, out!
: Okay, girls — how about we take five and rendezvous when I’m done having a talk with Maya about our upcoming sexual encounter?

: There will be no upcoming sexual encounter! And this will take a lot longer than five minutes! That isn’t nearly enough time to chop your corpse into pieces I can easily distribute throughout the shrine grounds!
: Now, that’s just mean. I don’t recall the old Maya ever threatening to kill me. She probably did at some point, though.
: What are you doing?! What is all this about?! I can get in trouble for you being here, you know!
: From who? God? I’ve never even seen another shrine maiden here.
: In fact, I’m not convinced this isn’t just your secret house that you’ve been hiding from everyone for Maya reasons.
: Where did you even get the dresses?!
: Don Quijote. They have everything there.
: Ayane-
: Don-don-don, donki! Donki...hōteeee! Boryūmu manten gekiyasu janguru~
: AYANE!
: Hi.
: What do you want?! Why are you here?! Do you just get a kick out of pissing me off or something?!
: No, I just miss you.
: ...What?
: I miss you. And I miss coming here on weekends to hang out and brainstorm and listen to your stories about the end of the world.

: And while I understand that it wasn’t you I was doing all of those things with, it doesn’t change the fact that you still look like her and act like her and get mad at me the same way she did when I’d come here unannounced.
: We used to joke back then...about what would happen if other girls started getting involved with all of this apocalypse stuff.
: How we’d all wind up as shrine maidens and how clean this place would be with the help of our entire class...
: You hated it back then too. You still thought I was annoying and pushy, but...
: A lot has changed since then. And I thought it would be nice to turn those old jokes into something real. Even if it’s for just...a few minutes before you kick us all out.
: I don’t...
: I don’t know what sort of relationship you have with me.
: I don’t know where the Maya I know starts or...where you begin. And that’s made it...really hard for me to accept the way things are now.
: I know you’ve found some closure with Sensei. And I’m happy for you guys...really.
: I never really...got that, though. So it’s still like my friend is just a new person all of a sudden and...
: I miss her sometimes.
: And I just thought that maybe, you’d like...miss me too or something. Whether it be subconsciously or...
: I don’t know.
: I’m just sorry.
: I always thought it’d be me to get sent back if it was either one of us, honestly.
: I wasn’t prepared for this. And now I don’t know what I’m supposed to do whenever I’m around you.
: I want to be there, though. Not just with you, but for you.
: And if Sensei can find it in himself to love you and look at you as your own person instead of a ghost of the past, then I can too. And I’m sorry it’s taken this long for me to try and do that.
: You...
: You don’t need to apologize. And I...can’t really tell you where I begin either since that’s just...a weird fucking question.
: It’s not like...we aren’t friends, though. Right?
: Like...we’re both always with Ami. And we probably met that way or something. But I can’t specifically remember where-
: That’s exactly the thing, Maya. Ami was barely even a part of it before you left. If anything, she was the one who started drifting away. It was always you and me until it just...wasn’t anymore.
: Those are the days I miss...
: And I want them back.
: What are-
: D...Do you really need to touch me for this?
: Yes. It’s symbolic. I’m showing you I won’t ever let go again.
: I want you. I need you. And I don’t want you to ever feel like you aren’t wanted or needed either when I know for a fact how hard things must be for you right now.
: I’m...fine, though.
: You can pretend all you want, but I know that if I’m handling this Niki situation poorly, it must be twice as bad for you. You’ve always been afraid of her. I know that much hasn’t changed.
: That’s...I don’t really want to...
: Let’s go back to normal. My normal. Not yours. The one where we secretly confide in each other and live a life that exists apart from just which one of us gets Sensei on any given day.

: I understand this is probably a weird and jarring thing to ask when you’ve never been that close to me from your perspective, but this is kind of how this all started in the first place. So I just need to do it again.
: I wore you down with love and attention and annoyance and you eventually caved and let me in. So I know you’ll do it again and I know cute things like this do get to you eventually.
: You’re just a normal teenage girl at the end of the day, aren’t you? We both are...So why are we always pretending to be something bigger?
: Why can’t we just cry when we want to cry? Scream when we want to scream? Lash out and punch our pillows as we curse the world for how cruel it is to us?
: I don’t want to always be strong. And that’s why I feel comfortable telling you now that I can’t do this alone anymore. I need you.
: You...have like four other girls out there already, though. Are they not enough?
: I’d trade all of them for you. Just please don’t tell any one of them I said that.
: Was I...was the old me really that important to you?
: Yes...she was. You were.
: But I’ve...
: I’ve never been that important to...anyone but Sensei before. I just don’t get how...things would even get to that point?
: Some of the strongest bonds are formed from people experiencing terrible things together.
: And even if you constantly insulted me...and teased me...and were willing to sacrifice me so long as it meant saving you, it didn’t matter. You were still my friend.
: So please...be that again. My real friend. Not just the other girl who hangs out with Ami.
: She’s so fucking crazy. Like, beyond clinically insane.
: Right?! And you were always the one I could talk to about that until you went poof and everything got bad! She’s so creepy and I have nobody to vent to about it anymore!
: What if I’m not...as good as the Maya you remember, though?
: What if you never wind up feeling like you can tell me anything or...what if I just never care as much as she did?
: Like, the only good friend I’ve ever had is Ami and I literally just trashed her behind her back. Who says I won’t do the same with you?
: You probably will. And maybe this is just ignorance on my end since the last Maya may have been super jaded after an eternity of misery, but I don’t think she or you ever meant or mean that stuff.
: I think you’re just as scared as me. And I think you should be allowed to feel that way instead of just suppressing it like we’ve both been doing for God-knows how long.
: I am struggling right now. And Sensei isn’t always there to make those feelings go away. But we can be that for each other, Maya. Salvation.
: That’s the gayest thing a straight girl has ever said.
: I think we’re supposed to kiss now.
: You really...won’t mind me?...
: Because I...doubt I’ll ever change. And I doubt I’ll be even...half the person you need or want me to be. But I...
: I am...lonely. And scared. And sad.
: I know.
: I’m so fucking sad...
: I know..
: Why did it have to be her?...
: What are we supposed to fucking do now?...
: Cry...
: We’ll cry and cry and cry until we run out of things to cry about. Then we’ll pick ourselves up and keep fighting to get out of here. To a world where we won’t have to do this anymore.
: Does a place like that really exist?...
: Is there somewhere out there for girls like us?...
: I don’t know...
: But I believe that...
: I believe that one day, there will be a place for everyone.
: And that it’s somewhere we’ll never find if we’re just stuck in here...
: Okay. It’s been thirty minutes. I’m getting out of here.
: I’ll be at Saizeriya if anybody needs me for some fucking reason.
: Okay. Thanks for coming, Yumi. Ayane’s not here to say it, but we both thank you for actually making somewhat of an effort to-
: Bite me. I’m gonna have fun burning this stupid dress.
: They’re totally doing it, right? No two girls can look at each other like that, disappear for thirty minutes, then come back sexually unsatisfied. It’s impossible.
: I don’t know how many times I need to tell you Ayane is straight until you believe it.
: I can hear it over and over again but she acts even gayer than I do sometimes.
: The longer I remain in this dress, the more I start to believe it is fusing to my skin.
: Okay. How about we just call it for today, then?
: Already? But we haven’t even done anything. I thought this was supposed to be our Rooftop Apocalypse Squad orientation?
: We’ll push orientation back until the next beach trip. I think Ayane’s tackling a more important mission at the moment.
: It better be sexual. I ship those two hard.
: Who do you ship me with?
: Makoto, obviously.
: Ugh.
: Nice.
: You’re both smart. You both wear glasses. And you’re both girls.
: That’s it?
: I’m easy to please. What can I say?
: I suppose I’ll try to catch up with Yumi since we’re leaving. Are you two coming along?
: Count me in. I’m friggin’ starving.
: Nodoka?
: I have something else to do, unfortunately. But thank you for the invitation.
: Suit yourself. Come on, Uta.
: Aye, aye, Captain Makoto! Or shall I say — Nodoka’s future wife?
: You shan’t. Ever again, for that matter.
When the clock strikes twelve, on gazing up, reflection matters slightly;
Some tell you it’s the journey scribing meaning to the plot.
I’ve been here since rather early. I can tell you that it’s not.
‘Tis the hands, you see. In lifting them, I change the present nightly.
How dull it is existing in a world that shines so brightly.
